name: 02-public-lifecycle-linux-and-real-oss
title: Public close -> DELETE -> retire -> collect, on a real Linux durable stack
subtitle: colima VM container · Spring jar + packaged Hosted Harness + durable local-process Broker · MySQL 8.4.11 · grace 10 s
lines: ## PR arm, fake OSS over TLS (real aliyun-sdk-oss 3.18.4); A = deleted, B = sibling Session left open
POST /close   202 -> completed  554 ms      capabilities after close: session_delete=true
DELETE        202 -> completed  292 ms      retirement gen=1; GET A/artifacts -> 404
+0.5 s   RETIRING  grace_period   held=13,641,895  oss=15/15
+10.5 s  DELETING  gen 1          (claimed when retired_at + grace became due)
++ +10.9 s  COLLECTED gen 1          held=0  collected_bytes=released_held_bytes=13,641,895  oss=0/15
++ OSS ledger: 15 DELETE, 15 distinct keys, max 1 per key, only A's keys; B untouched and still reads (sha256 ok)
== 16 GetBucketVersioning probes for 15 deletes (one per page + one per key inside deleteIfPresent)
## main 623cfc67, same public lifecycle (no collector)
!! after DELETE: RETIRING for the whole 90 s window, 17/17 objects and 13,929,258 held bytes retained
## PR arm against a REAL Aliyun OSS temporary bucket (private, unversioned, created and deleted for this run)
++ A: 8/8 objects present -> 0/8; claimed +11.1 s, COLLECTED +11.7 s after retirement; bucket 16 -> 8 objects
++ B: 8/8 present, PINNED, full + range reads still 200 with the right sha256
++ versioning Enabled on the real bucket -> 2 attempts, 0 DELETE, 4/4 objects kept:
==     IllegalStateException: Tool publication bucket cannot enforce immutable objects
== cleanup: 12 object versions + bucket deleted; NoSuchBucket confirmed; keys never printed or written to the rig dir
note: On macOS the Workspace close path is unavailable (durable worker identity needs /proc and /etc/machine-id), so every retirement scenario ran in the Linux container through the public API.

name: 03-blockers-and-siblings
title: Blocked publications keep objects and quota; siblings in the same Session are still collected
subtitle: Same Linux stack, public lifecycle; tenant held bytes sampled before/after
lines: ## Q: one Session, two Shell calls in one Turn = two publications
flip one bit in an OSS object of pub#1 -> public download 503 artifact_unavailable -> pub#1 quarantined (production path)
++ after DELETE: pub#1 RETIRING / quarantined   objects 7/7  held 6,296,459 kept
++              pub#2 COLLECTED                  objects 0/7  held 0
## W: write_evidence = FALSE (pre-upgrade publication)  ->  RETIRING / legacy_write_evidence_missing, 7/7 kept
## P2: journal recovery not READY when DELETE runs      ->  retirement recovery_protected=1, 7/7 kept
## R2: live read lease left by a crashed reader (40 s left at retirement)
+0.8 s grace_period (next in 9.2 s)   +11.1 s reader_active (next in 59.7 s)   +71.2 s COLLECTED
## unknown PUT: one injected PUT 500; the next attempt RETURNED and all 11 objects are VERIFIED
!! put attempts RETURNED=7 UNKNOWN=1  ->  after DELETE: RETIRING / put_unresolved, held 6,296,450, never collected
!! nothing in the code moves UNKNOWN -> RETURNED (design: 'permanently blocks automatic collection until externally resolved')
note: Injected by SQL (no public trigger exists): W write_evidence, P2 recovery_status, R2 lease row. In Q the bit flip is applied to the stored object; detecting it and quarantining are production code, as is the PUT 500 handling.

name: 04-storage-faults
title: Storage faults: one wire request per DELETE, the page is retried as a whole, quota is released once
subtitle: Fault injected on the 5th DELETE of one publication; ledger from the OSS double; Linux stack, grace 10 s
lines: == case                      attempt 1                           retry                                       DELETE requests  released once
++ DELETE 500 InternalError  4 deleted; key#5 -> 500, 1 request  +70.6 s gen 2; keys 0-3 -> 204              12 (7 keys)      6,296,458
++ DELETE reset (no reply)   4 deleted; key#5 reset, 1 request   +70.5 s gen 2; keys 0-3 -> 204              12 (7 keys)      6,296,464
++ versioning Suspended      0 DELETE; collection_retry x2       restored -> +130.9 s gen 3                  9 (9 keys)       6,585,156
++ kill -9 Spring mid-page   key#5 DELETE held; Spring killed    restart waits 59.6 s claim; +71.5 s gen 2   12 (7 keys)      6,296,455
++ 113 OSS keys = 2 pages    page 1 -> cursor segment:stdout:84  page 2 next tick; 1.7 s total               113 (113 keys)   117,456,030
++ 2 live Spring collectors  3 Sessions deleted together         both owners active; 1 owner per pub, gen 1  93 (93 keys)     3 x 31,464,656
== retried keys answer 204 (object already gone); no SDK-level replay of any DELETE
== GetBucketVersioning probes: 115 for the 113-key publication (one per page + one per key inside deleteIfPresent)
note: Exceptions defer the whole page by 60 s under the owner/generation fence; idempotent deleteIfPresent makes the repeat harmless.

name: 05-f2-download-cost
title: F2: download SQL cost and the fixed 120 s read lease (+5 ms per DB request packet)
subtitle: Public full download of one Shell artifact; TCP relay in front of MySQL delays every client->server packet
lines: == arm                    SQL per MiB  40 MiB @ +5 ms           100 MiB @ +5 ms          128 MiB @ +5 ms
-- main 623cfc67          711.4        cut at 24.2 MiB (120 s)  -                        -
!! PR (88d4ca9466 tree)   205.0        complete in 55.5 s       cut at 85.8 MiB (120 s)  cut at 87.3 MiB (120 s)
++ PR + 2-line candidate  38.8         complete in 10.3 s       -                        complete in 31.3 s
## where the PR arm's 205/MiB goes (general_log, 40 MiB): per 64 KiB response chunk ~11 statements
2,396 read-lease checks · 2,105 managed_agent_session · 2,105 managed_workspace_access · 1,463 publication receipt
= ManagedArtifactService 64 KiB write loop (lease + access) + VerifiedStream.read 64 KiB cap (guard before and after)
## candidate: those two 64 KiB constants -> 1 MiB (same granularity the PR already uses in the store path)
## stop after revoke / retire mid-download (OSS GET throttled to 4 MiB/s, action at 8 MiB)
PR arm:    revoke -> +0.64 MiB then aborted     DELETE -> +0.21 MiB then aborted
candidate: revoke -> +0.88 MiB then aborted     DELETE -> +0.02 MiB then aborted
note: The PR fixes the store-side amplification (3.5x fewer statements). The body's '100 MiB completes in ~108 s at 5 ms' did not reproduce here: 100 MiB was cut at 85.8 MiB.
